notes: Annotated typescript, manuscript page 3, archive sheet number 11 (comment only). No new title, date or total page count. There are five displays and no diagram or drawing.

The page writes the map (*) on higher direct images, its H¹(S,−) map (**), and a fibrewise map (* bis). It asserts that the vanishing of (*) (equivalently the fibrewise homomorphism) forces u(x)=0 through the stated compatibility. All three readers checked only the conditional zero-map consequence under functoriality and that compatibility; the construction and fibrewise detection were not proved.

Section 2 considers i:Y→X for proper smooth schemes over an algebraically closed field and rational coefficient cohomology in degree 2n−1. The live word propres is a mixed type/pen correction of projectifs. Both Q coefficients are pen corrections over typed Z. In a), the page assumes an algebraic reverse map that is a right inverse on the image of i*. The reverse-map label looks most like vk, with v* and v^* retained as alternatives; a mathematical expectation of an asterisk does not settle it.

For the conditional algebraic check, write r:A→B and v:B→A. A right inverse on im(r) means rvr=r. The readers checked the domains and, where stated in their events, (vr)²=vr and (rv)²=rv. This does not prove existence or algebraicity of v. The first R degree remains 2/a-shaped; the same damaged impression governs later recurrences and is not restored solely from degree expectations.

The NB calls the hypothesis a special case of “conjectures standart” and says “donc est sans doute touhours vérifiée”. It next asserts the hyperplane case when Lambda on the cohomology of X is algebraic and says this can be verified “par exemple lorsque X se remonte en car. zéro avec sa polarisation.” Sweep S, row 36/12 (n°2 a), NB) [A36-01], challenges this as a confusion between hard Lefschetz and algebraicity of Lambda. The ink confirms the lifting/polarization assertion; its mathematical correction is recorded as S’s objection, not substituted into the transcription or independently certified here.

Main inspection found the old d under r in opération, omitted by C/H and by two readers. It resolved old j in the cancellation after de and old ce beneath propriété. The terminal hook of propriété connects to its insertion guide and is not transcribed as a separate comma. Cancellation x characters are distinguished from recovered underlying old letters. The opening oa/ou, the order of overlapping u/v impressions in aurons, both layers of homomorphisme, and the exact pen/typed extent at final s in propres remain uncertain.

H’s opening global note already records the typewriter chi-shaped ell, and its emph macro represents authorial emphasis. Those conventions alone are not counted as new errors; actual underline extent, false typed-Q provenance, and omitted old letters are compared. H’s explanatory note about the unnamed structural morphism g is recognized as editorial and not misclassified as authorial text absent from the scan.
overview: Three fresh complete readings were compared. Main adjudication inspected thirteen existing reader crops and seven new local crops. The final separates literal source shapes, uncertain correction chronology, and mathematical expectations. H global notation/editorial conventions are credited before error counts.
